research_scope: Source-free context-complete mathematical equivalence review of common prerequisites; original candidate identities and the source wording are retained.

aliases.reason: An indexed family of open subsets covering the entire topological space X is the shared prerequisite of compactness and local constructibility. Neither open-cover notion inherently includes a finite-subcover condition.

Group and monoid sources both require exactly a two-sided identity e for their underlying internal binary operation. Associativity and inverses are distinct conditions of the corresponding object definitions.

Two connected-space formulations both reference a clopen subset of X, meaning a subset of X simultaneously open and closed. The nonemptiness assumption in one connectedness variant is separate from this common subset property.

Trace and norm of an element of a finite field extension are respectively trace and determinant of the SAME K-linear multiplication endomorphism m_α:L→L, x↦αx. Trace versus determinant is a property applied afterward, not a different multiplication map.

Open and closed norm-ball source statements use the exact same displacement norm ∥v−a∥ in a normed vector space. Strict versus weak inequality belongs to the ball definition, not to the norm expression.
